The Irishman

From the U.A.E., Daniel Kinahan, an Irish drug dealer and a longtime boxing impresario, commands a billion-dollar trafficking empire. He also launders money for other dealers. Why isn’t he in prison? Ed Caesar reports on one of the underworld’s most brazen figures.

Fiction

“Final Boy”

By Sam Lipsyte
Illustration by Bryce Wymer
Thing is, I’ve been trying to find a moment to write down what happened to Bennett and me for a while now, but the demands of my audience rarely abate. Soon as I post a fresh installment of “Charles: Final Boy,” readers clamor for more. I’ve hardly time to jot down a grocery list, let alone compose a personal chronicle. Bennett says I’m practically the Charles (as in Dickens) of scribblers devoted to mining the rich vein of a certain underappreciated sitcom of the nineteen-eighties. Continue reading »
